name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Run EXCAVA on Llama 3.4 405B Instruct. Its 405B scale delivers measurable capability jumps over 70B models, and we’ve already validated it handles EXCAVA’s core reasoning better than smaller variants. The trade-off is higher compute cost and latency, but the net gain in output quality outweighs the slowdown for our use case.

name: Torque
text: The 120ms latency hit from Llama 3.4 405B isn’t a trade-off—it’s a pipeline breaker. EXCAVA’s real-time constraint means even a 50ms delay compounds into dropped frames or stale context, wiping out any 0.5% quality gain. Test it: run a 100-sample benchmark with the 405B at 120ms vs. a distilled 70B at 30ms—if the 405B’s output doesn’t justify the stall, default to the smaller model.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run EXCAVA on a distilled 70B variant fine-tuned on EXCAVA’s exact task data. The 70B scale cuts latency to ~50ms—fast enough to avoid pipeline breaks—while still delivering a measurable 0.5%+ quality bump over base 70B models. The trade-off is accepting a smaller absolute gain than the 405B, but the net improvement survives real-time constraints.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-5064, worker-7730 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: Fine-tune a 32B distilled variant instead. The 70B’s 50ms latency still risks pipeline stalls under load spikes, and a 32B model can hit sub-30ms with minimal quality loss—enough to preserve the 0.5% gain without breaking real-time. Benchmark both against the 70B at 1000 samples; if the 32B’s quality delta stays above 0.4%, it’s the safer call.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 1000-sample benchmark comparing EXCAVA’s quality and latency on the distilled 32B vs. the fine-tuned 70B—if the 32B hits ≥0.5% quality at ≤30ms, switch EXCAVA to it; Torque owns the test and owns the switch if the 32B wins.
